description: The Indus Valley Civilization is a Bronze Age civilization that developed primarily in the northwestern regions of the Indian Subcontinent. It is renowned for its excellent town planning, advanced drainage system, and the extensive use of baked bricks.

sections.title: Introduction and Chronology
sections.description: Crucial historical facts regarding the timeline and discovery of the Indus Valley Civilization.

key_concepts.explanation: A period in history for which written records exist, but the script remains undeciphered.
A historical period characterized by the use of bronze, an alloy made by smelting copper and tin.

historical_events.significance: The most developed and urbanized phase of the civilization, according to Radiocarbon (C-14) dating.
The first site discovered by Daya Ram Sahni, which led to the naming of the culture as the Harappan Civilization.
Discovered by R. D. Banerjee, this major site's name literally translates to the 'Mound of the Dead'.

sections.title: Major Sites and Geographical Position
sections.description: Important cities of the civilization, their river locations, and key archaeological findings.

geographical_data.key_characteristics: Findings include the Great Bath, the Great Granary, and the famous Bronze Dancing Girl statue.

geographical_data.key_characteristics: Yielded evidence of a ploughed field, fire altars, and camel bones.

key_associations.extra_info: It is the only Indus city discovered without a citadel.

sections.title: Town Planning and Architecture
sections.description: The structural layout of the cities and scientific building techniques.

key_concepts.explanation: City streets intersected each other at right angles, dividing the town into distinct rectangular blocks.
Cities were typically divided into an elevated 'Citadel' for public buildings/ruling class, and a 'Lower Town' for common habitation.
Highly advanced underground network of covered drains built with baked bricks, connected to almost every house.

important_facts.fact: Doors and windows of houses generally opened into back alleys rather than the main streets, with Lothal being the only exception.
The standardized ratio of the baked bricks used in construction was 4:2:1 (Length:Breadth:Thickness).

sections.title: Society, Economy and Religion
sections.description: Social life, trade mechanisms, and religious beliefs of the Indus Valley people.

key_concepts.explanation: Internal and external trade was conducted through the exchange of goods without the use of metallic currency.
The abundance of terracotta figurines representing the Mother Goddess suggests a female-centric or matriarchal social structure.

key_associations.extra_info: The term used in contemporary Mesopotamian inscriptions to refer to the Indus Valley Civilization.
The Indus people were the first to cultivate cotton; the ancient Greeks referred to it as 'Sindon'.
A steatite seal from Mohenjo-Daro depicting a seated figure surrounded by four animals (elephant, tiger, rhino, buffalo) and two deer at its feet.

important_facts.fact: The Indus Valley people were completely unaware of iron; it strictly remained a Bronze Age culture.
Their system of weights and measures was highly standardized, based on multiples of 16 (16, 64, 160, etc.).

sections.title: Script and Decline
sections.description: Details about their writing style and the various theories explaining the civilization's mysterious collapse.

key_concepts.explanation: A script composed of symbols and pictures, written alternatively from right to left on the first line and left to right on the second line.
A theory proposed by Mortimer Wheeler suggesting that foreign invasions by Aryans destroyed the civilization (now largely rejected).
The most widely accepted modern theory attributing the decline to shifting river courses, frequent flooding, and climate change.

important_facts.fact: The Indus Script has not been completely deciphered to this day, keeping the civilization classified under the Proto-Historic period.
The Swastika symbol is believed to have originated from the Indus Valley Civilization.
